prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1082; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision in which the claimant's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic light. The claimant reports a wrist fracture and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time of the loss, with nothing indicating a lapse or a start date after the accident.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene. The responding officer's notes are consistent with the rear impact described.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the collision happened as the claimant described it. Scene photographs and two independent witness statements match the same sequence of events.

Entry 5: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The rear damage pattern and crush depth are consistent with the impact described, and no prior damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 6: Claimant's account of the collision and of the injury was given again today and matches the initial report in every detail. No prior injury to the wrist or surrounding area is known from the claimant's history.

Entry 7: The reported wrist fracture is consistent with the force of a rear impact of this type, based on the vehicle damage and the claimant's position in the car. Imaging from the emergency visit is on file.

Entry 8: Treatment has continued since the initial visit, with additional appointments and several new services added over the following weeks. The volume of care is higher than I would expect for a fracture of this type, so I have flagged the file for medical review.

Entry 9: Medical review requested the complete treatment records and billing history, and the request is pending. No changes to coverage are recommended at this time.

Entry 10: Next step is to receive the full treatment records and reconcile the services billed against the documented injury. Reserves will be reviewed once the medical review is complete.
